programs.title: Library of known results
programs.goal: Formalize known results so that every program builds on checked ground.

programs.title: Geometric complexity theory
programs.goal: Attack lower bounds through orbit closures and representation theoretic obstructions.

programs.title: Circuit lower bounds via algorithms
programs.goal: Turn faster satisfiability and learning algorithms into circuit lower bounds.

programs.title: Proof complexity
programs.goal: Prove lower bounds on proof length in stronger and stronger proof systems.

programs.title: Meta-complexity
programs.goal: Study the hardness of problems that are themselves about complexity.

programs.title: P = NP algorithm search
programs.goal: Search for a polynomial time algorithm for an NP-complete problem. Any hit is held back under the security rule in ISOLATION.md.

attack.title: Table: the exact cost of representing each small bipartite graph by a circuit of two-input AND and OR gates
attack.why: An exact table of small cases computed with outside contributors, each entry a statement with a certificate; by a lemma in print, a bound past a linear threshold in this measure for one explicit graph would give a bound for circuits with NOT gates.

attack.title: Table: exact least size of two-input AND/OR circuits for the edge functions of small graphs, with and without NOT gates
attack.why: An exact table of small cases, to find the smallest graph on which a NOT gate saves a gate; for sixteen small graphs the sizes without NOT gates are checked and the matching bounds with NOT gates are conjectures being checked.

attack.title: What a lower-bound method for representing a graph could be that does not eliminate gates one at a time
attack.why: Three seats for one day, each naming an object and computing it on the small tables before arguing; several objects have been tried and dropped with reasons.

attack.title: A fresh look at turning a faster circuit-analysis algorithm into a lower bound
attack.why: A one-day look by two seats at where the earlier candidate algorithms did not look; three objects tried and dropped, one narrower place named.

attack.title: Where a fast algorithm could hide that the earlier eliminations did not cover
attack.why: A one-day look by two seats; one concrete kind, cancellation built from constant-size gadgets, was run on a small family and eliminated at the sizes tried.

attack.title: Conjectures stated in the complexity literature, each begun as one exact table of small cases
attack.why: At most five conjectures, each read at its source and each with a stated consequence for circuits with NOT gates; one that shows nothing after its first table is dropped that day.

attack.title: Conjecture: on graphs with no 4-cycle, some least AND/OR circuit of two-input gates has only clean AND gates
attack.why: Checked: the size bound when every AND gate is clean, that on bipartite graphs a least circuit never has exactly one AND gate that is not clean, and moves that remove such a gate with an exact gate count; the open step, a conjecture, is that some such gate can always be removed at no larger size, and all of it concerns circuits with no NOT gate.

attack.title: A price for incidences that a circuit re-reads at both the point and the line
attack.why: Checked: a size inequality on planes with the count of such incidences, and a normal form for least circuits. A count meant to join them was broken by our own seats (by script, not checked), and on paper that count is the main target again.

attack.title: AND/OR circuits where every incident pair has a proof reading its point and its line at most twice: a size bound
attack.why: Stopped: checked, from an outside proof: on a plane of order q with N points such circuits of two-input gates have at least N q / 100 gates. The line moved on.

attack.title: Conjecture: with two-input AND/OR gates and no NOT gate, a plane's incidence function needs more than linear size
attack.why: The main target of this line, a statement about circuits with no NOT gate; a bound here does not by itself say anything about circuits with NOT gates.

attack.title: AND/OR circuits of two-input gates where every incident pair is reached reading its line once or its point once
attack.why: A rung between the checked case and the first line, argued on paper from a checked count for sums of sets; its own row is not filed yet, it waits on one definition.

attack.title: AND/OR circuits of two-input gates with few AND gates whose two inputs both depend on lines
attack.why: Checked counts for a restricted class and one conjecture that joins them; the count loses a factor for each such gate, which is the wall the first line must pass.

attack.title: Rejecting the largest false inputs: what a circuit must do on inputs with many points and lines on
attack.why: Every cheap circuit on file accepts these inputs (by script, not checked); the question is what rejecting a fraction of them costs.

attack.title: Conjecture: on graphs with no short cycle, AND/OR circuits of two-input gates need gates linear in the number of edges
attack.why: The graph form of the main target; cuts made by outside contributors through the reduction door are being built and sent to the checker.

attack.title: The exact circuit size of the Petersen graph's edge function when NOT gates are allowed
attack.why: The test case for graphs of maximum degree three, cut into cases by the first gates; six of the eight cases for the graph minus a vertex are checked.

attack.title: Conjecture: graphs of maximum degree 3 with no short cycle need edges plus cover minus one gates, NOT gates allowed
attack.why: The cubic case needs a new step at a vertex of degree three; the leaf step is checked.

attack.title: The atlas: exact least circuit sizes of small graphs and small pieces of planes
attack.why: Data to read before guessing a law; lower bounds are checked only up to a measured size, the rest is listed as computed.

attack.title: New measures of a circuit, each a definition with sanity lemmas and its values on the atlas
attack.why: A measure is kept only if it predicts sizes on the atlas where gate counts and covers do not.

attack.title: One NOT gate on the line functions of a plane (several outputs)
attack.why: Stopped: its end statement is of a kind already known for several outputs, so it does not move the one-output question.

attack.title: Circuits with few NOT gates computing several outputs
attack.why: Stopped: checked for every plane given as data, and a statement of this kind for several outputs is already known.

attack.title: AND/OR circuits of two-input gates of bounded line-degree
attack.why: Stopped: line-degree three is checked, and climbing one degree at a time only changes constants.

attack.title: AND/OR lists of two-input gates whose line tests are right on arcs
attack.why: Stopped: its end statement prices only a circuit shape already covered, and every per-line count tried on it failed on an explicit circuit (by script, not checked).

attack.title: Monotone formula depth of small graphs and gadgets
attack.why: Stopped: every probe came back on the expected side, so the space holds no surprise at these sizes.

attack.title: Permanent against determinant: linear spaces on which the permanent stays constant
attack.why: No seat is on it; two small probes remain on the desk.

attack.title: Proof complexity: lower bounds for proof systems
attack.why: No seat is on it since its seats moved to the one-output question.

attack.title: The search for a fast algorithm for satisfiability
attack.why: Three candidate ideas did not survive their tests on the record; its seat now searches for small circuits on the one-output question.

attack.title: Local reductions and the minimum circuit size problem
attack.why: Parked: its checked rows restate a known idea on our definitions.
